question: Magnetic field is a quantity that has ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**both magnitude and direction**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• A **magnetic field** is defined as a **vector quantity**, which by definition means it possesses both **magnitude** (strength) and **direction**. 
 
• The **magnitude** of a magnetic field refers to the intensity of the magnetic force at a specific point. In the **International System of Units (SI)**, the magnitude is measured in **Tesla (T)**. Another common unit used is the **Gauss (G)**, where **1 Tesla** is equal to **10,000 Gauss**. 
 
• The **direction** of the magnetic field at any point is the direction in which the **north pole** of a compass needle points when placed at that location. Outside a magnet, the field lines emerge from the **North Pole** and enter the **South Pole**.
